packageRules.description: VanillaBP and the adapters follow the framework, not Renovate: their versions are bumped when a release is cut, and while they are snapshots there is nothing to look up. The Camunda 7 adapter of the module migration-tests is one of them.
Operaton fixes only its newest minor, with a patch every month, and this adapter follows it (decision 4 in DECISIONS.md). A patch comes in on its own.

A new Operaton minor never merges itself. Renovate only proposes it, and a person decides when the adapter moves on: the adapter uses engine classes under '.impl.', which Operaton may change in any minor, and an application has to upgrade its database with it. The job 'client-configuration' of checks.yaml lists on the pull request which settings the new version adds. Milestones and release candidates are left to the nightly build against the next Operaton.

java-uuid-generator follows the engine, not Renovate. operaton-engine 2.2 is built against 5.2.0 and declares it 'provided', so the adapter brings exactly that version, although the Camunda 7 adapter brings 4.3.0. Raise it together with a new Operaton minor, to the version that operaton-engine names. bin/sync-from-camunda7.sh keeps the version of main.
